title: The Metasploit Framework: Democratizing Penetration Testing
summary: The evolution of the Metasploit Framework, from H. D. Moore's open-source project to a powerful platform that made exploit development and penetration testing accessible.
whyThisMatters: The evolution of the Metasploit Framework, from H. D. Moore's open-source project to a powerful platform that made exploit development and penetration testing accessible.

sections.overview:
In 2003, H. D. Moore started the Metasploit Project as a portable network game in Perl. However, it quickly evolved into a powerful tool for exploit development and execution. The goal was to create a public, open-source resource for researching security vulnerabilities and developing code that allows a computer user to take control of a remote computer system.

The release of Metasploit Framework 2.0 in 2004, rewritten in Ruby, was a landmark event. It provided a reliable, plug-in-based architecture that allowed the security community to contribute their own exploits, payloads, and tools. This 'democratized' hacking, making advanced penetration testing techniques accessible to a wider audience, from security professionals to hobbyists.

In 2009, the project was acquired by Rapid7, a cybersecurity company. This acquisition provided the resources for full-time development, leading to the creation of commercial versions like Metasploit Pro, while the core Framework remains open-source. It is now the world's most widely used penetration testing framework.
